name: 229. A virtual key edited between requests still counts every request (vk-edit-usage) [SERIAL]
description: TXE-5272. Editing a virtual key reloads it into the governance store, and the reload kept the key's rate-limit usage by loading the live counters, copying them into the reloaded config and storing it. A request charged in between (usage is charged after the response, off the request path) was overwritten, so a key edited under traffic undercounted and let requests past its limit. The prerequest creates a run-scoped key limited to 4 requests an hour, spends all 4 on openai/gpt-4o-mini (3 tokens each) and edits the key after each one; the row reads the key back and its test script sends the fifth request, which must be refused with the key's own request limit at 4/4. Red before the fix whenever an edit overwrote a charge (intermittent, since it depends on that interleaving); green after. The key is deleted at the end. Spends four gpt-4o-mini calls of 3 tokens. Run with FEATURE=vk-edit-usage.
